question_interpretation: Asks what Part 101 requires of the principal display panel (PDP) of packaged food: its definition and area, what must be placed on it, and the type-size/prominence rules tied to it.

issues.detail: J lists the PDP definition/area, information panel, type size and prominence (all supported by 101.1 and 101.2), but omits what the PDP itself must bear: the statement of identity (101.3(a), bold, parallel to base, 101.3(d)) and the net quantity of contents (101.7(a),(e),(f): distinct item in the bottom 30 percent, type size keyed to PDP area in 101.7(i)). The PDP-area definition in 101.1 exists precisely to set the 101.7(i) net-quantity type size.

The 1/16-inch minimum type size in J comes from 101.2(c) and applies to information on the PDP or information panel; the duplication of mandatory information on alternate PDPs (101.1) is also a PDP requirement not listed.

explanation: 101.1 and 101.2 support every element listed in J, so nothing in the key is wrong. However, a question about PDP requirements is incomplete without the two mandatory PDP declarations (statement of identity and net quantity of contents), which 101.3(a) and 101.7(a) place on the PDP. proposed_corrected_answer: PDP = label part most likely displayed under customary retail conditions; must be large enough for all mandatory PDP information without obscuring/crowding; information duplicated on alternate PDPs; PDP area = height x width (rectangular), 40% of height x circumference (cylindrical), 40% of total surface otherwise (excluding tops, bottoms, flanges, shoulders, necks). Information panel = panel immediately contiguous and to the right of the PDP (101.2(a)); 101.4/101.5/101.9 etc. information on PDP or information panel (101.2(b)); minimum 1/16-inch type, prominent and conspicuous (101.2(c); 101.15).

question_interpretation: Asks what small-package labeling exemptions and alternative formats exist in Part 101.

issues.detail: The question is scoped to Part 101, but G cites only 101.9(j). Part 101 also contains small-package alternatives for dietary supplements (101.36(i)(2): 101.9(j)(13) applies with 4.5-point/6-point minimum type sizes) and general small-label alternatives (101.2(c)(2): individual serving packages <=3 sq in may use 1/32-inch type; 101.2(f): alternative methods by regulation). 101.7(f) also relaxes net-quantity placement for PDPs <=5 sq in.

The <12 sq in exemption is conditional on no nutrition claims and on providing an address or telephone number for nutrition information (101.9(j)(13)(i)(A)); the firm-size (j)(1) and low-volume (j)(18) exemptions are not package-size based but are fairly included.

explanation: 101.9(j) supports every J element: exemption for packages with <12 sq in available label area, tabular/linear displays for <=40 sq in, retailer firm-size exemption (j)(1), and low-volume exemption notice (j)(18)(iv). But the question asks for small-package exemptions and alternatives in Part 101 as a whole, and 101.36(i)(2) and 101.2(c)(2)/(f) are Part 101 small-package provisions the key does not cite.
proposed_corrected_answer: Nutrition labeling: packages with <12 sq in available label area exempt if no nutrition claims/information, but must bear an address or phone number for nutrition information (101.9(j)(13)(i)); packages <=40 sq in may use tabular or (if tabular will not fit) linear formats, abbreviations, and any label panel (101.9(j)(13)(ii)); alternate panels for >40 sq in packages lacking space (101.9(j)(17)); retailer firm-size exemption (101.9(j)(1)) and small-business low-volume exemption with notice to FDA (101.9(j)(18)). Dietary supplements: 101.9(j)(13) applies with 4.5-point (small) / 6-point (intermediate) minimum type (101.36(i)(2)). General: 1/32-inch type for restaurant/institution single-serving packages <=3 sq in (101.2(c)(2)); alternatives by regulation for labels too small (101.2(f)); net-quantity bottom-30% placement waived for PDPs <=5 sq in (101.7(f)).

question_interpretation: Asks to distinguish authorized health claims, qualified health claims and structure/function claims.

issues.detail: Qualified health claims are not provided for anywhere in 21 CFR Part 101 (no occurrence of 'qualified health claim'); they rest on FDA enforcement discretion and guidance following court decisions, with FDA letters specifying qualifying language. J lists 'qualified claim disclaimers' alongside regulatory requirements without saying that these are not codified, so an answer that cites a Part 101 regulation for them would be fabricating.

J's 'structure/function notification and disclaimer' applies only to dietary supplements (FD&C 403(r)(6); 21 CFR 101.93). Structure/function claims on conventional foods require no notification or disclaimer; the key does not distinguish them.

The statutory bases FD&C 403(r)(1)(B)/(r)(3) (health claims, including FDAMA authoritative-statement claims 403(r)(3)(C)) and 403(r)(6) (supplement S/F statements) are not cited; authorized claims are listed in 101.72-101.83.

explanation: 101.14(c) supports the significant scientific agreement standard; 101.70 sets the petition process; 101.93 supports the S/F notification and disclaimer. Two distinctions are blurred, though. Qualified health claims have no codified Part 101 requirement (they are a guidance and enforcement-discretion framework), and the S/F notification and disclaimer rules apply only to dietary supplements.

explanation: FD&C 605 = 21 U.S.C. 364a (verified). J's 15-business-day deadline, records retention and label contact information are all correct. The key omits the follow-up new-medical-information reports, the label copy and the fragrance-ingredient request, and the retention period. The label-contact requirement itself sits in 609(a).
proposed_corrected_answer: The responsible person must submit to FDA every serious adverse event report received for use of its cosmetic in the U.S. (605(a)), with a copy of the label, no later than 15 business days after receipt (605(b)(1)); submit new and material medical information received within 1 year of the initial report within 15 business days (605(b)(2)); receive reports via the domestic address, domestic phone or electronic contact on the label (605(d); label requirement in 609(a)); keep records of all adverse event reports for 6 years (3 years for qualifying small businesses) and allow FDA inspection (605(e)); provide fragrance/flavor ingredient lists within 30 days of an FDA request (605(f)). 'Serious adverse event' defined in 604(5).

evidence.quote: The responsible person shall submit to the Secretary a serious adverse event report accompanied by a copy of the label on or within the retail packaging of such cosmetic product no later than 15 business days after the report is received by the responsible person.
evidence.issuing_authority: U.S. Code (OLRC/GPO)

evidence.quote: The responsible person shall submit to the Secretary any new and material medical information, related to a serious adverse event report submitted to the Secretary in accordance with paragraph (1), that is received by the responsible person within 1 year of the initial report to the Secretary, no later than 15 business days after such information is received by such responsible person.
evidence.issuing_authority: U.S. Code (OLRC/GPO)

evidence.quote: for a period of 6 years, except that a responsible person that is considered a small business for the purposes of section 364h of this title, who does not engage in the manufacturing or processing of the cosmetic products described in subsection 364h(b) of this title, shall maintain such records for a period of 3 years.
evidence.issuing_authority: U.S. Code (OLRC/GPO)

evidence.quote: Each cosmetic product shall bear a label that includes a domestic address, domestic phone number, or electronic contact information, which may include a website, through which the responsible person can receive adverse event reports with respect to such cosmetic product.
evidence.issuing_authority: U.S. Code (OLRC/GPO)

rubric_fairness: fair in part — G is correct for the core; an answer citing 609(a) for the label requirement is correct but not anticipated.
